messages.author: d25ec8b43762536f
messages.subject: Error in microclimate(), probably in .Fortran().
parts:
Dear all,
I'm trying to calculate microclimate data for a particular area by using microclimate().

It's a big data, so I used two computers (both Win10 64-bit) to do the calculations for me and used the same input data with the same code (only the file paths were changed).

Unfortunately, however, one of the computers had an error without sending any error reports or warnings which the results were ridiculously out of whack. For example the calculated soil surface temperature can reach 1.28784026045517e-311.
Strangely, the results from the other computer were all fine.

After comparing the codes, I determined that the input data were exactly the same, but every time after microclimate (micro), there was a problem with its results.
Moreover, after using .Fortran() from the microclimate source code, I get errors as a result.

What I want to ask is, 1) What is the reason for this error? 2) How should I solve this problem?

Thank you,
Linxuan Ma

messages.author: d25ec8b43762536f
messages.subject: Re: Error in microclimate(), probably in .Fortran().
parts:
Dear all,

In order to determine the specific cause of this error, I then used two other new computers to run the same code. The result is very surprising, all computers have the above error. By comparing the errant computers with computer running correctly, I found that these computers had the latest version of R as well as the latest version of NicheMapR.

Next, I first installed an older version of the R on my computer and then ran the code. Unfortunately, this error still occurs.

Then I installed an older version of NicheMapR (3.2.1) for R. Finally, all the computers were running normally.

To sum up, I speculate that the latest version of NicheMapR may have errors in microclimate() related functions that will not report errors. 
Dear Kearney, you can try to fix this bug.

In addition, if any friends have the same problem, you can try to reinstall the old version of NicheMapR first. code show as below:
remove.packages("NichemapR")
devtools::install_github('mrke/NichemapR@5017e1f') #Testing this version works.

Thank you,
Linxuan Ma

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Error in microclimate(), probably in .Fortran().
parts:
Dear Linxuan Ma,
It sounds like you're not using one of the 'micro_' functions but setting up your own call to 'microclimate' by specifying all the inputs manually. You need to be careful doing this because if you miss anything or get an input vector or matrix's dimension wrong, you'll have issues because Fortran won't tell you and will proceed to use memory in an inappropriate way and input will get out of alignment. If you send your code I can take a quick look to see where the problem might be.
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: 与“Error in microclimate(), probably in .Fortran().”相关的私人帖子
parts:
Hi Linxuan Ma,

I see where the problem is - you are missing some new values that need to go into microinput. You must have based your script on an older vignette. You need to add these:
"spinup, dewrain, moiststep, maxsurf" to the end of microinput. You can put the following values for them:
spinup <- 1 # repeat first day 3 times for steady state
dewrain <- 0 # don't feed dew back into soil as rain
moiststep <- 360 # how many steps within the hour is soil moisture solved over
maxsurf <- 95 # what is the maximum allowable soil surface temp (for stability purposes), deg C

The reason you see different behaviour on different systems is probably because of different default compiler settings. I've seen lots of weird things like that, e.g. a situation where you specify a variable declared to be single precision real as an integer, e.g. 1 instead of 1.0, and when compiled on a PC it makes no difference while on a Mac it causes a segfault.

All the best,
Mike

It sounds like you're not using one of the 'micro_' functions but setting up your own call to 'microclimate' by specifying all the inputs manually. You need to be careful doing this because if you miss anything or get an input vector or matrix's dimension wrong, you'll have issues because Fortran won't tell you and will proceed to use memory in an inappropriate way and input will get out of alignment. If you send your code I can take a quick look to see where the problem might be.
All the best,
Mike
